title: Browser multiplayer weapon game across four repositories

input.summary: Build a browser Three.js multiplayer weapon game where a valid kill earns part of a token-backed prize. The server, indexer, frontend, and v4 contracts may be separate GitHub repositories.

user.outcome: The browser game, server, indexer, and contracts can be reviewed as one multi-repository project. Gameplay stays offchain; only authenticated, reserve-bounded results may create token claims.
user.status: Design waits on kill authority. Fee scope is unresolved. No source, application, deployment, provider support, or public game exists yet.

decision.question: Who has final authority to declare that a kill is valid and may create a reward?

options.label: Authoritative game server
options.consequence: Fastest and simplest, with disclosed operator trust and server-side anti-cheat controls.

options.label: Independent signer quorum
options.consequence: Reduces one-key control but adds operators, latency, coordination, and recovery work.

options.label: Verifiable result proof
options.consequence: Reduces server trust only if a practical proof system can cover the complete game result.

user.nextAction: After this answer I will freeze the trust model, repo graph, funded reward lifecycle, typed result schema, failure rules, and exact test obligations.

facts.statement: Players use a browser-based Three.js client for a real-time multiplayer weapon game.
A valid player kill awards part of a token-backed prize to the winner.
The game server, indexer, web client, and contract package may use separate public GitHub repositories.
The initial design uses a sponsor-funded reserve and no player entry fee or wager.
The accountable source that makes a kill valid and reward-bearing is not confirmed.

architecture: The Three.js client renders, predicts, captures input, links a wallet, and never becomes reward authority.
The authoritative game service validates movement, shots, hits, kills, match limits, disconnects, and replay-resistant result records.
A contract package holds the funded reward reserve, verifies typed results, rejects replay, and lets beneficiaries pull finalized claims.
The v4 hook remains isolated from gameplay and receives no fee or callback behavior until canonical execution scope is confirmed.
The indexer derives chain state with reorg rollback and freshness disclosure; it never decides winners or reserve solvency.
Application V3 uses the contract repository as primary and content-binds every companion repository, schema, test, dependency, and runtime asset.

findings.effect: Different result authorities change cheating risk, key custody, liveness, and when a reward becomes enforceable.
findings.repair: Confirm one result-authority model before selecting signatures, server topology, or claim settlement.

findings.effect: Future swap volume cannot back a reward promised for a completed kill.
findings.repair: Reserve the complete match liability before reward-bearing play; use realized fees only for future budgets.

findings.effect: A test or receipt in one repository cannot prove source or behavior in another repository.
findings.repair: Bind every repository by numeric identity, commit, root tree, source closure, build profile, tests, and evidence.

evidence.meaning: The synthetic forward-test preserves the complete multi-surface game request.
No public repositories, commits, source manifests, dependency locks, or CI runs exist.
No game server, chain deployment, indexer, browser runtime, provider lane, or monitoring has been exercised.

gates.reason: The game experience, reward trigger, and separate repository surfaces are preserved.
Kill-result authority is a material unresolved owner choice.
No source exists and implementation must wait for the confirmed trust model.
No clean public GitHub revision or complete multi-repository closure exists.
Deployment, provider integration, legal review, operations, and public activation are independent later gates.
